claims.text: The strong low-field magnetocaloric response is governed by a balance between chemical disorder and local magnetic exchange interactions.
An optimized level of atomic disorder produces a continuous, second-order-like magnetic transition rather than an abrupt first-order transition.
The proposed disorder–exchange balance enhances magnetic entropy change at low applied fields.
A continuous, second-order-like transition limits magnetic hysteresis.
The proposed disorder–exchange balance preserves rapid heat exchange.
The proposed disorder–exchange balance preserves mechanical robustness.
The baseline alloy has a near-equiatomic composition and a partially disordered crystal structure.
Increasing Co concentration relative to the baseline modifies local magnetic exchange interactions.
Atomic-scale chemical disorder forms a percolative network of local magnetic clusters.
A percolative network of local magnetic clusters ensures a smooth magnetic transition.
A controlled increase in Co concentration refines the distribution of exchange interactions.
Refining the distribution of exchange interactions softens the magnetic transition and lowers hysteresis.
Increasing Co concentration amplifies the magnetocaloric entropy change.
Increasing Co concentration can tune magnetic responsiveness without compromising thermal or mechanical performance.
Relative to the baseline, the Co-enhanced alloy will exhibit a larger isothermal entropy change at low applied fields.
Relative to the baseline, the Co-enhanced alloy will maintain low magnetic hysteresis and fast heat exchange.
The proposed mechanism applies to rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys in a regime where minor transition-metal adjustments tune exchange interactions.
The proposed mechanism applies particularly at room temperature and under low-field magnetic-refrigeration conditions.
